metadata.title: Teachers Getting the Best out of Their Students (EN)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The report is based on TALIS 2018 teacher and principal questionnaires administered in primary (ISCED 1) and upper secondary (ISCED 3) education, with participation being optional for the primary and upper secondary modules. The publication explicitly describes the use of teacher and school weights and complex variables/scales in Annex B, and notes that principals’ responses are usually weighted by school weights, while in some cases principals’ answers are analysed at the teacher level and weighted by teacher weights. The report also states that TALIS results are based exclusively on self-reports and that no data imputation from administrative data or other studies is conducted. Because this is a descriptive policy report (not an ML prediction study), the manuscript does not provide a single ML-specific weighting variable name (e.g., W_FSTUWT) in the extracted text; analysts should follow the TALIS 2018 technical documentation for the exact weight variables and complex survey variance estimation approach.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This publication does not analyse cognitive achievement outcomes with plausible values; instead it reports descriptive and regression-based associations for teacher and principal self-reports (e.g., motivations, training, preparedness, working conditions, stress, intentions). TALIS uses questionnaire scales and complex survey design features, but the extracted text does not describe any plausible-value generation or PV-based scoring for the reported outcomes. Missing data handling is therefore not specified in the extracted sections because the report focuses on survey item non-response/adjudication categories and reporting conventions rather than an ML pipeline requiring explicit missing-data imputation rules.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report uses TALIS 2018 teacher and principal samples for ISCED level 1 (primary) and ISCED level 3 (upper secondary). Participation in the primary and upper secondary modules is optional by country/economy; the report includes 15 primary participants (with adjudicated data available for 13) and 11 upper secondary participants. The report also applies TALIS adjudication rules for inclusion in international averages and for reporting (e.g., minimum numbers of schools/teachers and item non-response thresholds), and excludes countries/economies that did not meet TALIS standard participation rates from international averages for specific educational levels. For some indicators, the analysis is further restricted to teachers teaching in target classes that are not directed entirely/mainly at students with special needs, and for some equity-related indicators the sample is restricted to teachers in schools with specified student composition (e.g., more than one cultural/ethnic background).

data.outcome_summary: This OECD report synthesizes TALIS 2018 teacher and principal questionnaire results across ISCED level 1 (primary) and ISCED level 3 (upper secondary), with lower secondary used mainly as a comparison point. The report is descriptive and policy-oriented: it reports percentages and cross-country comparisons for themes such as teacher motivations, training and preparedness (including transitions and play in primary), instructional time allocation, professional development and feedback, school leadership and collaboration, and teacher well-being and stress. It also references regression-based associations and gap decomposition analyses, but the extracted text does not specify any machine-learning predictive modeling, target variables, or ML performance metrics. The report emphasizes that TALIS is cross-sectional and based on self-reports, so causality cannot be inferred. Methodologically, it highlights TALIS adjudication/reporting conventions and the use of teacher and school weights and complex variables/scales, while noting that no imputation from administrative data is conducted.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is an OECD TALIS 2018 synthesis/report that does not present an empirical machine-learning prediction pipeline with defined ML target variables, algorithms, or performance metrics in the extracted sections. As a result, ML-specific fields (ml_techniques, main_findings structured for predictive targets) are intentionally left empty, and the extraction focuses on the survey design and reporting conventions described in the technical annexes.
